label: Early copy phase of short sequences (outputs 1-2, absolute step <= 6)
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase (99.7% of mass), on the first two copy steps after the delimiter step (recall_idx 1 and 2; 97% of mass), and only when those steps are early in absolute time: t <= 6, i.e. L=3 or 4 (both recall steps) and L=5 (recall_idx 1 only). Strongest on the step right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, 61% of mass) in L=3-4 sequences; top activations are all L=3 at recall_idx 1, with recall_idx 2 weaker (~0.5-0.8 of max). Rate falls off steeply with L: L=6+ almost never fires. Token identity matters little (h/r inputs mildly higher). Does not fire on the delimiter step, the recall_idx 0 output, later copy steps, or the original phase (except a faint 2% rate at t=1). Misses are mostly weak activations at L=5 recall_idx 2 (t=7) and small tails at later steps; false positives are mostly L=5.

issues: Count recall is only 0.71. The roughly 29% of active steps the predicate misses carry just 7% of the activation mass, and they are spread thin: L=5 recall_idx 2 (t=7), L=4 recall_idx 3 (t=7), copy-phase tails at t>=8, and a sparse t=1 original-phase blip. None of these is a strong systematic class.

The t<=6 cutoff is a proxy for 'L<=4, or L=5 recall_idx 1'. Firing actually tapers with L and recall_idx; it does not cut off sharply at an absolute step. The L=5 cells are partial: recall_idx 1 has precision 0.74 and recall_idx 2 has precision 0.32. That is why most false positives are L=5 recall_idx 1.
The token preference (inputs h and r) is weak. h/r inputs outside the predicate have precision of only about 0.16, so this does not form a missed class.
Alternatives I tested did not beat the original: L<=4 & recall_idx<=2 (F1 0.687), recall_idx<=2 & L<=5 (F1 0.779), adding t==7 & L==4 (F1 0.753), recall_idx<=2 & t<=7 (F1 0.694).
skeptic.revised_label: Fires on copy outputs 1-2 (right after <DEL>) in short sequences (L=3-4, plus L=5 output 1); falls off quickly as L grows
